original_value: QNSTOP consists of serial and parallel (OpenMP) Fortran 2003 codes for the quasi-Newton stochastic optimization method of Castle and Trosset for stochastic search problems. A complete description of QNSTOP for both local search with stochastic objective and global search with “noisy” deterministic objective is given here, to the best of our knowledge, for the first time. For stochastic search problems, some convergence theory exists for particular algorithmic choices and parameter values. Both the parallel driver subroutine, which offers several parallel decomposition strategies, and the serial driver subroutine can be used for local stochastic search or global deterministic search, based on an input switch. Some performance data for computational systems biology problems is given.

result.paraphrase: QNSTOP includes serial and parallel OpenMP Fortran 2003 implementations of Castle and Trosset’s quasi-Newton stochastic optimization method for stochastic search problems. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first complete description of QNSTOP for both local search with stochastic objective functions and global search with “noisy” deterministic objectives. For stochastic search problems, convergence theory is available for certain algorithmic choices and parameter settings. An input switch determines whether the parallel driver subroutine, which supports multiple parallel decomposition strategies, or the serial driver subroutine is used for local stochastic search or global deterministic search. Performance results for computational systems biology problems are also presented.
